newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada legislators urge relax of foreign bank rules.
newsitem.headline: Canada legislators urge relax of foreign bank rules.

text.p: Foreign banks should be given freer access to Canada's banking market, including the option of opening branches to provide more competition to the country's six big banks, Canadian legislators said Thursday.
Canada should join other industrialised countries in lifting broad restrictions on the way foreign banks operate, said the finance committee of Canada's unelected upper house.

"The committee's proposal to clear the way for foreign banks to carry on wholesale banking activities in Canada will create a more competitive domestic banking environment," the committee's deputy chairman, Sen. David Angus, said in a statement.
The finance committee of the House of Commons, the country's elected chamber of Parliament, issued a similar report on Thursday.
In recent years, several foreign banks abandoned Canada because of its restrictive banking laws and stiffer than expected competition from the domestic banks.
Under current rules, offshore banks must set up a federally regulated subsidiary with its own capital, board of directors and audit system.
The number of foreign banks operating in Canada has dropped from a peak of over 60 to 43 institutions today.
The committee reports go farther than the federal government's white paper on financial reforms released earlier this year which suggested minor changes to foreign bank rules.
Canada's Bank Act, the legislation which regulates the country's financial services industry, is up for review in 1997.
In its white paper, the federal government proposed allowing foreign banks to opt out of paying deposit insurance under the federal Canada Deposit Insurance Corp.
The white paper did not allow offshore banks to open Canadian branches with access to their parent firms' capital.

In their reports, the finance committees said foreign banks should be able to compete for business loans under a less regulated branch structure. But offshore banks must still pay their fair share of taxes, including capital taxes.

"While the committee strongly recommends quick access to direct branching, we do not wish to provide foreign banks with an unfair competitive advantage over Canadian banks," the House of Commons finance committee said in its report.

Foreign bankers welcomed the finance committee reports and suggested banks that have shied away from Canada may give the country a second look if the changes are adopted by the federal government in its bank act review.

"With greater flexibility in the way they can structure their Canadian operations, foreign banks can be expected to increase their already important role in trade finance, corporate lending, loans syndication and capital markets," said Fred Buhler, chief executive of BankAmerica Corp.'s Canadian subsidiary.
